title: EVEN THE BUILDING DRESSED UP. (every flat is invited. the guests wear green.)
format: reel (1080x1920, H.264 High, 30 fps, yuv420p, +faststart, 18.5 s, baked foley over a continuous ambience bed in AAC 48 kHz stereo) with a designed 1080x1920 cover; grid tile = cover y 240-1680
caption:
Even the building dressed up. The lights went up from the terrace to the gate, and every flat is invited.

The guests wear green: the Baguette Tennis Necklace, 36 cm, ₹2,099; the Baguette Tennis Bracelet, about 17 cm, ₹1,599; and the Baguette Huggies, ₹1,199 a pair. Green baguette cubic zirconia, 18k gold tone plated. Also in ruby-red and crystal.

The building, window by window: Shop 1, back in five minutes. Shop 2, no soap required. The gate, the watchman knows. 103, the window seat. 102, tamarind and lemon. 101, one bulb is always out. 203, kahi nako. 202, two necklaces. The landing, one earring. The terrace, rehearsals, the moon, and tonight.

The lights come down next week. The pieces stay. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

[ the green set · 18k gold tone plated · see you on the terrace ]
first_comment: Twelve windows, one building, every light on. Thank you for coming up. Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #WeddingGuest #TennisNecklace #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: An illustrated pink Art Deco apartment building at night, every window lit, a pink paper lantern at each one and an almost-full moon over the terrace. Strands of warm fairy lights unfurl from the roof down the whole building, and the name panel on the stepped crown at the top left lights up with the Naira wordmark. The camera rises to that corner of the terrace: the lantern hanging under the crown, a swag of lights, and on the terrace wall a fold of blush silk with a gold border. Drawn first as cream outlines in the dark, three pieces come into the light: a pair of huggie earrings, a tennis bracelet and a tennis necklace whose length falls over the edge of the wall, all set with green baguette stones, 18k gold tone plated. The words EVEN THE BUILDING DRESSED UP rise beside the lantern, 'every flat is invited. the guests wear green.' The camera pulls back to the whole building lit and dressed in lights, and ends on a card: the green set, Baguette Tennis Necklace ₹2,099, Baguette Tennis Bracelet ₹1,599, Baguette Huggies ₹1,199, green cubic zirconia, 18k gold tone plated, nairaflore.com, 'the lights come down. the pieces stay.'
sound: In-app instrumental, no vocals: a wedding brass-band or shehnai-style tune played softly, as if from the street below (search 'indian wedding band instrumental', 'shehnai instrumental'), rising under the lights from 1.0 s; if only vocal versions exist, a warm string-ensemble instrumental instead. Duck it 4 dB under the foley. Baked (reel.mp4's own track, AAC 48 kHz stereo, peak -20.7 dBFS): under everything, 0-18.5 s, a continuous bed of the building's evening, distant traffic hum and a far crowd murmur at -53 dBFS, looped seamlessly at 18.5 -> 0 s; 0.0-1.7 s the street and a distant wedding crowd a little closer; 0.6 s the lift-bell (one soft brass stroke, ~1.2 s decay); 1.0-4.3 s a soft rising shimmer, cresting at 3.6 s and falling away under the click; 4.0 s a warm switch click (the crown lights); 7.8 s one glass chime (the first glint); 14.6 s the end-card chime.

The set spans tile x 69-1018 (949 px); at 1.20 the frame holds 900 px of tile, so a piece is cut by the frame edge, and the brief's focal (560, 950) put 'EVEN THE' above the 290 word line. Toward the centre (540, 960) the push also carried the tile 180 px up the screen: the crown's wordmark rose to y 128-232, under Instagram's top bar, and the lowest 30 % of the frame was empty plaster (review fix 4). At 10.6 s now (p12/_build/measure.cjs): wordmark y 302-388, 'EVEN THE' top 502, the turns' bottom 948, the necklace's tail 1503 and the silk's foot 1506 (inside 1630); the set keeps 16 px either side. The push is composed over C-CAMERA in the kit's own form (exponential scale, the focal point on a straight line, cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) over 7.6-10.6 s) and unwinds with e on the pull-back, so the two moves meet with zero velocity; the headline's 16 px rise at 8.0-9.5 s now reads on its own, not on an upward camera drift.

THE SILK graded to blush: p12/assets/AI-19-blush.png from kit/plates/AI-19-clean.png (p12/_build/silk.py, Lab: cloth L' = 81 + .85 (L - 69), a' = .80 a + 1.2, b' = .58 b; the gold zari, Lab hue > 58 deg and chroma > 26, kept and lifted 3 L; alpha untouched). The cleaned plate's cloth measured Lab 69 / 15.7 / 18.2 (salmon, hue 49 deg) and read taupe-tan on the rose parapet, a banned ground; it now reads as the brief's blush raw silk (median #EAC0B7) and separates from the parapet by its lightness. Only the bay's own image source changed; the shared plate is untouched.

C-OUTLINE (review fix 5): each connected piece's alpha is CLOSED with a 17 px disc, blurred sigma 3.5, traced at 0.5, simplified at 4 native px, given two Chaikin passes and then smoothed along its own length (Gaussian, sigma 14 native px, the path resampled every 2 px) in p12/_build/trace.py. Two steps go beyond the review's recipe, both to meet its acceptance: (1) each piece is closed on its own, because the two huggies lie 24.7 native px apart and one 17 px closing over both bridged them into a single blob; (2) the length smoothing, because the recipe alone still left the rounded top of every baguette along the far side of the necklace's loop as a ~1.4 screen px wave at the stone pitch (~42 native px; seen at 2x in the 6.0 s frame), which a closing cannot remove (they are bumps, not gaps). Sharp turns (over 35 deg in 20 native px of path): necklace 26 -> 3 (the three left are the real notch where the fall passes under the loop, now a soft S, and the tail's two crop corners, which lie under the silk's turned-up corner), huggies 16 / 8 / 5 -> 0 / 0 / 1, bracelet 5 / 2 -> 0 / 0. The line stays on the piece's edge: its centre is never more than 2.7 screen px inside the alpha at 1.10 where it crosses the top of a stone (under its own 3.3 px width), and 3.5 px once, at the necklace's tail just above the flap. Viewed at 2x at 6.0 and 6.4 s: no scallop on the loop's top, the fall's left edge or either hoop. The line softens to half strength as it retracts and the necklace's line stops under the silk's turned-up corner (a clip at tile x 740-870, y > 1213), as before.

THE DUSK: the brief's 'three cream outlines in the dark' needs a dark ground, and the terrace ledge is light plaster under the strings. A warm dusky-rose multiply (#A6828F, feathered) lies on the ledge, the coping and the silk's fall at .85 and, since review fix 6, down the parapet face (tile y 1046-1376) at .55, under the parapet strands (inserted before them), full to y 1310 and feathered to nothing by 1410 in the string course; the flat ledge top no longer sits darker than a bright face below it, and at establishing scale the crown corner reads as a dark corner, not a stripe with a lump of silk in it. Both ease 15 % as the crown's own lights come on (1.2-3.0 s) and lift with the bloom (6.4-7.3 s): the face layer is the ledge's dusk x .55 / .85, so it follows the same curve. It is there from frame 0, so the crown corner is the one dark corner of the establishing frame ('only the crown corner is dark'). The bay's CLOSED state is unchanged (no dusk, nothing on the ledge), so every other post's establishing frame keeps the world's look; the reel drives the bay through h.p12.apply(). Round 3, fix 5: its right edge fades linearly to nothing over tile x 1000-1080 on all three dusk layers (ledge, coping and silk's fall, parapet face; a mask in each layer), so it no longer stops on a vertical line at the bay joint across a ledge that runs on into P11's lit one, which read at establishing scale as a pasted rectangle. Measured at frame 0 (s0): the step across tile x 1080 was 66 levels on the ledge and 69 on the coping; now 17 and 4, the joint's own drawn line. The silk ends at x 1020 and stays almost wholly in the dusk. CLOSED and LIT unchanged (the dusk is 0 in both).

THE SILK lies on the ledge in the dusk from frame 0 rather than appearing during the reel: a silk fading in from nothing would be the one magic event in the film. CLOSED (other reels) still shows the ledge bare.

WEDDING STRANDS in the reel are the world's 26 (setScene wedding 0 -> 1 over 1.0-4.6 s); the crown's hang from the crest's soffit through the sky until the headline comes. The bay adds three invisible occluders (.nv-occ): the ledge and coping band (y 798-1046), so a strand from the crest ends at the ledge's far edge (it hangs on behind the parapet: the crest stands on the terrace) and none crosses the set; the silk's own silhouette (p12/_build/occ.py), so the coping strands pass behind the silk's fall and the necklace on it; and (round 3, fix 4) x 120-210, y 260-1046, so the world's crown strand at x 165 no longer hangs just behind the kandil's right edge and down between its tails and through its halo (the emblem looked strung on a wire); its parapet copy below the coping stays, and the crown carries four strands, 290 / 415 / 540 / 665. THE HEADLINE'S HOLES (round 3, fix 3): the world cuts each strand to the words' own outlines, which left 2-3-bulb stubs between the crown's underside and 'EVEN THE' and under the turns, began the strand under 'UP.' on a half bulb and ended each glow copy on a hard horizontal edge. So after every world mask rebuild the reel takes the world's glyph hole for this bay's words out of the mask and cuts the crown's four strands itself, BETWEEN bulbs: a bulb goes under a line when the world's own glyph hole for that line (alpha dilated 17 px, blurred 1.6, at its place or 16 px lower, where it starts its rise) reaches the bulb's 7 px glow dot (p12/_build/holes.cjs renders each line's hole alone and reads every bulb's place on the world's '0 24' dash; holes.py writes the table into reel.html). Each cut sits at the midpoint between two bulbs, 12 px from each, feathered linearly over 10 px, so it never touches a bulb (radius 3.5) and the glow copy and haze fade out instead of stopping on a line. A run of fewer than 5 bulbs left between two cuts, or between a cut and the crown's underside or the ledge, goes with them; so once the words are in, 290 / 415 / 540 are clear from the crown to the ledge (the sky behind the text block reads clear, as on the cover) and 665 keeps its 6 bulbs from below 'UP.' down to the ledge (19 bulbs were hidden on each of 290-540, 15 on 665). The holes still follow the words: each bulb's hole is as deep as the most visible line that covers it, a removed run as deep as the shallower of its two ends, and a run that becomes shorter than 5 while the lines arrive (below 'every flat is invited.' before 'the guests wear green.' starts) goes as deep as its shallower end from 0, so nothing waits in the strands for words that have not come and nothing hangs as a stub until the next line comes. The world mask is rebuilt after the camera on every frame the camera's e, the veil's amount, a line or the set's develop changes (final render; see the mask check), so its holes sit on the pieces and words of every bay as they stand; world.js is untouched.

THE DRESSED BUILDING AT ESTABLISHING SCALE (review fix 7, eased in round 3, fix 6): at s0 the 26 strands were 2.3 px dots in a ~4.6 px glow and the finished building read as faint dotted rules. For this reel only, while the camera is under scale 0.5, each wedding strand's glow copy goes 14 -> 18 px and opacity .60 -> .75 (the review's figure), and the masonry's warm screen 8 % -> 10 %; the boost eases out (sine) between scale 0.40 and 0.60, so 1.0-4.6 s and the 12.8-14.6 s hold carry it and the close-up keeps the world's own strands. Round 2 had gone to 21 px / .90 / 12 %: at the hold the 26 strands merged into peach bars at phone width and crossed the other bays' headlines. Against frame 0, the share of the 13.5 s frame lifted by more than 30 (summed RGB) levels went 30.3 % -> 26.4 % (any one channel over 30: 10.2 % -> 8.5 %), and the 3.75 s frame 25.6 % -> 22.7 %; viewed at 360 px wide, the bulbs read as dotted light and 'TWO NECKLACES.', 'NO SOAP REQUIRED.' and 'LOST:' read through them. setScene has no hook for this, so reel.html sets it on the world's own markup after each frame's setScene and camera (the shared strand.js and world.js are untouched). FLAGGED to the world lead: a setScene({ weddingGlow, weddingWarm }) parameter would carry it without touching the DOM.

COVER vs REEL HOLD: the cover keeps the brief's cleaner cut (the bay's own six strands from the coping and the swag, the sky clear behind the headline), with the six strands carried on down the veiled landing below the tile; the reel's close-up carries the world's wedding curtain, with the sky behind the text block now clear too once the words are in (round 3, fix 3): of the crown's strands only 665's last 6 bulbs, from below 'UP.' to the ledge, stay in the sky, and three more parapet strands hang below the silk.

THE BLOOM ('the nearest strands' bulbs bloom, glow 1 -> 1.3') is a bay-level warm light (screen #FFC98A): a pool on the ledge where the set lies, light on the silk and a soft glow down the top of each parapet strand, rising over 6.4-7.3 s UNDER the pieces so the jewellery keeps its own colour. The world's strand layer is shared and was not touched. It stays on in LIT, so the cover's ledge carries the strings' light. The swag's own haze (a 40 px #FFC98A stroke at 12 % on the swag's curve, blurred sd 22) has its own filter in USER space, x 560-1200, y 90-410 (>= 4 sd past the stroke on every side), and lies under a copy of the swag's x 1046-1068 fade, so it falls off to nothing in the sky and at the pole (final review, fix 1; checks).

THE CROWN'S SPAN of the far wire is painted dark until 1.25 s, then bulb by bulb from the crest outward (90 ms apart, 140 ms each), in reel.html after each NVW.tick, as P10's reel did: the world lights the whole wire once P10 is lit.

GLINT band sweeps from just outside the piece to just outside it on the far side (background position 80 % -> 20 % on the 300 % background, a sine ease, narrow band .50 at its core), not the kit's 120 % -> -20 % under an in-out ease, which spent two thirds of the beat off the piece and crossed the piece itself in about 0.16 s (a flash); a broader .70 band washed the green stones to mint as it passed. The necklace's band runs DOWN it (168 deg: along the loop, then down the fall), the bracelet's and the huggies' across (105 deg).

PIECE SHADOWS: one tight silhouette shadow on all three (drop-shadow 0 5 px 6 px .28 + 0 1.5 px 2 px .24, rgba(40,16,30)) instead of the kit .cut's 18 / 22 px drop, which floats a piece lying flat; contact ellipses (multiply 32-34 %) under each huggie (the upright hoop at its foot, the lying one along its length) and the bracelet's near rim. The draped necklace's contact is its silhouette shadow only: an ellipse cannot follow a chain over a fold.

END CARD drawn on the kit's card (ground #E3B2A6 with the plaster at 20 %, the 760 x 220 brass plate, the flower turning on the I's stem at 36 deg/s) with the brief's P12 layout set in this reel (the kit's layout has one name and one price): product lines Jost 500 34 px tracked .06 em, the bracket Cormorant 38, every line inside 860 px (widest 807 px, the service line; 'BAGUETTE TENNIS BRACELET · ₹1,599' 669 px). SOUND: the baked track is synthesized (p12/_build/sfx.py): a continuous bed of the building's evening under everything, 0-18.5 s (distant traffic hum and a far crowd murmur, -53.3 dBFS RMS, every 100 ms window -55.2 to -51.8 dBFS, rendered 0.6 s long and crossfaded equal-power into its own head so 18.5 s runs into 0 s unbroken: the seam's sample step 0.00041 against a 99th-percentile step of 0.00067), so the reel is never digital zero; over it the street and a distant wedding crowd 0-1.7 s, the lift-bell 0.6 s, a rising shimmer 1.0-4.3 s, a switch click 4.0 s, a glass chime 7.8 s, the end-card chime 14.6 s (moved with the card, round 3, fix 1). Round 3, fix 2, the click that could not be heard: the shimmer's onsets now run 1.0-4.15 s under an envelope that crests it at 3.6 s, takes it 10 dB down by 4.0 s (linear in dB) and to nothing by 4.3 s, so it recedes under the click instead of cresting on it; and the click is 5 dB up (-26 -> -21). In 5 ms windows (RMS over both channels, 1 ms hop) the click now peaks at -32.6 dBFS and the loudest window of everything else in 3.8-4.2 s is -41.9 dBFS: 9.2 dB under it unrounded (5 ms peak windows: -23.4 against -32.7, 9.3 dB). On the round-2 track, the same measure gave the click's window -36.4 dBFS against the shimmer's -35.7 in 3.75-4.0 s. Track peak -20.7 dBFS (the end-card chime's crest; the rule is <= -18). No music is baked.
